name: Nicholas Arcolano
bio: Head of AI & Research at Jellyfish, building AI agents and data platforms that help software engineering organizations measure and navigate AI transformation at scale. Leveraging massive real-world data sets to study what's working (and what's not) about AI tool and agent use across the industry, and sharing these learnings through published research and benchmarks so engineering leaders can make confident, evidence-based decisions. Harvard Ph.D., previously at TrueMotion (CMT), Runkeeper, MIT Lincoln Laboratory.

sessions.scheduled_title: Tokenmaxxing is the New "Lines of Code"

positions.claim: Code is now the fastest way to produce any asset, not just software — including video, websites, slides, and images.
Structure, not taste, is the expensive and scarce input in AI-assisted content production.
Almost no organizations actually maintain the PR hygiene, tagging, and internal documentation that AI-generated content quality depends on.
AI agents cannot solve organizational problems without documentation or skills to draw on, regardless of model quality.
Success with AI is increasingly decoupled from being the smartest or most technically skilled person in the room, and instead depends on conscientiousness.
Most AI skills currently published are low quality because they were generated without regard for their contents or structure.
2027 will be the year of the 'content engineer,' following 2026 as the year of the creative technologist.
Teams with the most disciplined software creation processes will also be the best-communicating teams.
Content was historically deprioritized not because it lacked value but because engineer time was too expensive to spend on it.
Fully code-generated product tours are not yet production-quality, but will become the norm.
